title: File-upload security
proves: Hostile files (spoofed extensions, HTML or script bytes, polyglot GIF/PNG/JPEG/WebP, pixel and decompression-bomb headers, active SVG, traversal names, a zip that inflates past its declared size) are refused by the shared upload guards; the antivirus hook works against a fake clamd (clean, infected, timeout, fail-open and fail-closed); chat media keys are not readable across tenants; CSV cells are formula-guarded; every upload route is size-capped, reviewed and on the shared policy (a new route fails the ratchet); on the booted API no upload-named operation accepts an unauthenticated upload.
doesNotProve: No authenticated live upload per route, no live cross-tenant HTTP download test (key ownership is tested in process), no real clamd, no real S3, no CSV import end to end, no JPEG trailer check beyond a markup scan (phone photos append data).
